question: Is converting CNY to USD, or wiring it out, itself taxed in China?
why_it_decides: This is the premise of the brief ('considerable taxes'). If the answer is no, the large number must be something else.
answer_today_blank_if_empty: No tax on the conversion or the wire was found in any official source read. The Regulation states that recurring international payments and transfers are not restricted; what the bank requires is a genuine lawful basis plus source/tax documents. The tax, if any, attaches to the underlying income — not to the act of converting.
how_to_discover: No discovery needed. If a bank or adviser quotes a 'conversion tax', ask them to name the tax, the charging document and the rate in writing (see Q10).

question: Does a U.S. passport holder get the USD 50,000-a-year ID-only purchase amount?
why_it_decides: It decides whether the simple yearly route (F07) exists at all.
answer_today_blank_if_empty: No. Under Art. 59 only a foreign individual holding the Foreign Permanent Resident ID gets the purchase convenience amount. A foreign passport holder buys FX from documented lawful current-account income (F01) with ID + source materials including tax evidence.
how_to_discover: No discovery needed — unless you also hold the PR-ID, in which case tell the bank (Q08).

question: Is USD 50,000 a hard annual cap on getting money out?
why_it_decides: A hard cap would force multi-year planning; a convenience threshold does not.
answer_today_blank_if_empty: No. The USD 50,000 figure is a convenience amount: inside it, ID alone suffices; above it, purchases/settlements proceed with transaction-amount source/purpose documents. Genuine lawful current-account and opened capital-account items have no amount limit in the Q&A.
how_to_discover: No discovery needed. Which documents your bank wants for your item is Q05/Q06.

question: What does the bank itself charge to convert and wire (Bank of China, today)?
why_it_decides: Separates the real, small bank cost from the feared tax.
answer_today_blank_if_empty: At today's BOC board the conversion spread versus the buy/sell midpoint is 0.2100% of the amount, and the published personal wire fee is 1‰ (CNY 50–260) + CNY 150 cable. Known bank cost: USD 53.42 at USD 10,000; USD 901.20 at USD 400,000 (one wire). Your own bank/branch price is Q11.
status: Answered for BOC today; your bank blank
how_to_discover: Use the Costs page for BOC; get your own bank's dated written quote (Q11).

question: Which Chinese tax rates could the 'considerable taxes' actually be?
why_it_decides: Names the candidates so the quote in Q10 can be checked line by line.
answer_today_blank_if_empty: From the IIT Law: comprehensive income (wages etc.) 3%–45% progressive; dividends, rent, property-transfer gain and incidental income 20% flat; business income 5%–35%. Property-transfer tax falls on the gain only (proceeds minus original value and reasonable costs). Which one applies to your money is Q06 — blank until the source of funds is known.
how_to_discover: Match the rate to your income type once Q06 is answered; confirm with the tax office that issues your 完税证明.

question: What created this RMB — salary, business profit, home sale, gift, inheritance, or money you brought in?
why_it_decides: Every lawful route is keyed to the source of funds. Without this, no route can honestly be recommended for your case.
status: Must be answered from your documents
how_to_discover: Bank statements for the account plus the document behind each large credit: employment contract/payslips, company distribution records, registered sale contract, gift/inheritance papers, or the inbound wire + exchange slip. Bring the bundle to the account-holding branch and ask which route (F01–F07) it will process.

question: Was Chinese tax already paid/withheld on that income — and can you prove it?
why_it_decides: Tax evidence (完税证明 / exemption certificate / tax-filing form) is part of the F01 document set; unpaid tax is the one large lawful cost found.
status: Must be answered from your documents
how_to_discover: Ask the payer for withholding records, or request your tax-payment certificate from the competent tax office (主管税务机关). If nothing was withheld, the IIT Law makes the taxpayer liable — settle before asking the bank to convert.

question: Under which ID is the account held, and how does the bank classify you (境外个人 vs 境内个人)? Do you hold a Foreign Permanent Resident ID or a cancelled hukou?
why_it_decides: Classification selects the rulebook (Art. 59 vs domestic-individual rules, F07 eligibility, F05/F06 eligibility). Official texts define 境内个人 two ways (Regulation Art. 52 residence test vs ID-based bank classification) — the bank's own record governs in practice, and the conflict is flagged.
status: Must be answered by your bank, in writing
how_to_discover: Ask the account branch: (1) which ID opened the account; (2) which personal category it has recorded; (3) whether a PR-ID or cancelled hukou is on file. Get the answer on bank letterhead — it decides F01 vs F07 vs F05/F06.

question: How much is there, in what currency mix, and when was the RMB acquired?
why_it_decides: Splits the job into 'already FX' (F03, cheapest), 'change-back within 24 months' (F02) and 'documented income' (F01); acquisition dates also set the U.S. currency-gain basis.
status: Must be answered from your documents
how_to_discover: Account statements showing currency sub-accounts and the date/rate of each acquisition; the original exchange slips (兑换水单) for anything converted in the last 24 months.

question: What exactly is the 'considerable amount of taxes' you were quoted — which tax, which office, what rate, on what base?
why_it_decides: No tax, rate, amount or assessing office is named in the brief. Until the quote is itemised it cannot be verified, negotiated, or credited in the U.S.
status: Must be answered by whoever quoted it
how_to_discover: Request the itemisation in writing: tax name, legal basis (document number), taxable base, rate, and the issuing office. Then check each line against Q05's rates and the Costs page. An unitemised percentage is not verifiable — treat it as blank.

question: What will your own bank (branch, channel, today) actually charge — rate, wire fee, intermediary and U.S. receiving fees?
why_it_decides: Every priced row here is Bank of China public tariff. Other banks, branch discretion, promotions, intermediary (OUR/SHA/BEN) and receiving-bank fees are not officially published as a single figure.
status: Must be answered by the banks, in writing
how_to_discover: Dated written quote from your branch for: the USD selling rate applied, the wire fee + cable, the charge option, and any intermediary deduction; plus your U.S. bank's incoming-wire fee schedule. Until then those cells stay blank — never assume zero.

question: What is your U.S. filing position — living in the U.S. or abroad, filing status, and were FBAR / Form 8938 filed for every year the account exceeded the thresholds?
why_it_decides: FBAR (over USD 10,000 aggregate) and Form 8938 (USD 50k/75k in the U.S.; USD 200k/300k abroad, unmarried) have separate penalties, and missed years change the plan before any money moves.
status: Must be answered from your filings
how_to_discover: List each year the China accounts exceeded USD 10,000 in aggregate and check a filed FinCEN Form 114 and, above the higher thresholds, Form 8938 for that year. Penalties if missed: FBAR non-willful up to USD 16,536; willful USD 165,353 or 50% of the balance; Form 8938 USD 10,000 rising to USD 60,000. Take advice before filing late — do not let the wire outrun the cure.

question: Did any part arrive as a gift or inheritance from a foreign person over USD 100,000 in one tax year?
why_it_decides: Triggers Form 3520 reporting (5% per month late, max 25%) and, for gifts without documents, no verified conversion route was found (flag).
status: Must be answered from your documents
how_to_discover: Aggregate gifts/bequests per donor per tax year. Over USD 100,000 from a nonresident alien/foreign estate: Form 3520 Part IV, each gift over USD 5,000 identified. For the conversion itself, ask the bank in writing whether the donor's own route (e.g. the donor remitting) is cleaner.

question: When did you acquire the RMB, at what rate — i.e. how large is the U.S. §988 currency gain on converting?
why_it_decides: Selling RMB is a disposition of nonfunctional currency. Gain is ordinary under §988(a) (Pub. 525's 'capital gain' wording conflicts — flagged); the personal-transaction exclusion only helps if the gain is USD 200 or less. On today's BOC selling rate, RMB acquired at the IRS 2024 average shows a gain of about USD 27,703 on a USD 400,000 conversion (gain, not tax — your marginal rate is Q15).
how_to_discover: Your acquisition dates/rates from statements (Q09) fix the basis. The Costs page illustrates the gain at IRS 2023/2024/2025 average acquisition rates for every USD 10,000 step; a U.S. adviser converts gain into tax.

question: What is your U.S. marginal position, and can Chinese tax paid be credited (Form 1116)?
why_it_decides: Turns the §988 gain and any Chinese tax into actual U.S. tax. No official page can answer this for an individual — any number here would be invented.
status: Must be answered by a U.S. tax adviser
how_to_discover: Bring the adviser: acquisition basis (Q14), Chinese tax certificates (Q07), and your filing status (Q12). Ask specifically about §988 character (ordinary vs the Pub. 525 wording), the USD 200 personal-transaction rule, and foreign-tax-credit eligibility.

question: How fast must the money be in the U.S., and is this one balance or recurring income?
why_it_decides: Speed eliminates routes honestly: F07 needs 8 years for USD 400,000, F10 needs 27 years, F11 needs 80 trips — while F01/F03 move the full amount in one wire once documents are ready.
status: Must be answered by you — no document settles it
how_to_discover: Decide the deadline first, then read the 'time' column on the Costs page. If the balance is recurring salary, set up F01 once and repeat it; do not stockpile RMB hoping for a simpler future rule (none is published).

question: Is any of the money company profit rather than personal money?
why_it_decides: Company profit has its own route (F09) and its own real tax (20% statutory; 10% treaty ceiling if eligible). Re-labelling personal savings as a dividend — or vice versa — creates the penalties on the Flagged page.
status: Must be answered from your documents
how_to_discover: Company accounts and distribution resolution showing genuine distributable profit; confirm with the tax office which rate (statutory vs treaty) it will apply and what residency proof it wants.
